transcript: A first preview. Literally decades in the making, chess is finally back on Broadway after 40 years. This is one of those things that has been rumored for so long. It feels like every year we would get a new rumor that chess was finally coming to Broadway. And now it's finally here, with an updated book by Danny Strong. Chess has had so many different scripts over the years, and I do think this is actually one of the more successful ones, although it's definitely still not perfect. I think one of the more divisive changes in this adaptation is going to be the character of the arbiter, played by Bryce Pinkham. In this version, he serves as an omniscient narrator who is very much aware that he's in a musical and makes a bunch of meta commentary throughout the piece. And a lot of that dialogue is very corny. I personally think they could dial it back a little bit, but the audience did seem to be eating it up. So another big change is giving someone else's story back to Florence, which is Leah Michelle's character. I actually don't mind that they gave her this song, and I think Leah sings it beautifully, but I do think the placement is a little odd, and it kind of comes out of nowhere. There's also a new song for set Lana, played by Hannah Cruz, who is excellent in her very limited stage time. The new song isn't great. But she sells it. I guess this is a good time to talk about the performances. I thought everyone was really solid, but the standout by far, in my opinion, is Nicholas Christopher. And I'm so glad that so many more people are now going to realize what a star he is. His song anthem, which ends Act one of the show, was my favourite song of the night, but I did like Aaron and Leah as well. The production itself is fairly minimal. It's basically a concert staging of the material, down to a lot of the costumes feeling very modern. There are some really cool choreography moments, although it's used pretty sparingly, as well as some video projection and some really great lighting design. All in all, I am really glad to see this score back on Broadway. The book is still not perfect, but to be honest, I don't think it's ever going to be. You're not really going to just for the story. You're going for the music. And the music is still as great as it's ever been, and sung by some really high caliber vocalists. And so in that respect, I think it's doing exactly what it needs to do.
